summary.text: A young woman presented with multiple nevi that began on the buttocks and spread to the back and legs over the previous 2 months. Examination showed hundreds of small dome-shaped reddish brown nevi on the legs and upper body, with a few newly formed lesions on the neck. She had no itching, bleeding, facial freckling or reported photosensitivity, no drug use, and no family genetic disease.

Dermatoscopy showed a reticular pattern, darker centrally and lighter peripherally, with peripheral globules. Histology of four lesions showed symmetric junctional pigmented melanocytic nests with spindle cells and pagetoid spread without atypia. S100, MelanA and HMB45 stained strongly positive, PRAME was negative and BAP-1 expression was retained, which excluded metastatic melanoma and BAP-1-loss Spitz nevi.

One larger lesion was excised for genetic analysis, which detected no HRAS mutation on next-generation sequencing and no ROS1 abnormality on FISH. Eruptive disseminated Spitz nevus was diagnosed from the clinical and pathological data, and strong sun protection with follow-up at 6-month intervals was recommended.
